title: Self-tensor augmentation for one two-term localization complex
statement: Let (C,J) be a small site, O a sheaf of commutative rings, and s a global section. Put L = [O -> O[1/s]] in degrees zero and one, with the actual localization differential and augmentation epsilon:L -> O[0] of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-extended-cech]. The ordinary total tensor map id_L tensor epsilon:L tensor L -> L tensor O[0] is a quasi-isomorphism. There is only one generator; the assertion has no arbitrary finite list or induction hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 099B, proof of lemma-derived-completion: the one-generator localization contraction

proof.text: Let P be the sectionwise localization presheaf and f:O -> P its unit. At every object, multiplication P tensor P -> P is an isomorphism by IsLocalization.bijective_linearMap_mul′, and (f tensor id) followed by multiplication is the left unitor. Thus f tensor id is an isomorphism. Apply the natural sheafification tensor comparison and the invertible sheafification counit on O to obtain that the actual sheaf map ringedSectionLocalizationUnit tensor id is an isomorphism. This computes the specified map, not merely an unspecified isomorphism between its endpoints.

The inclusion S[degree 1] -> L and the specified augmentation L -> O[degree 0] form a degreewise split sequence: in degree zero the projection is invertible, in degree one the inclusion is invertible, and outside these degrees all objects are zero. For any degreewise split sequence of complexes, total tensor with L is short exact: form its degreewise retraction and section by the total coproduct universal property, and check the splitting identities on every tensor summand.

Tensor L with S in degree zero. The resulting termwise tensor complex is supported in degrees zero and one; its differential is the map of step 1 conjugated by the canonical degree identifications, hence is invertible. Exactness in degree zero follows from its being mono, and in degree one from its being epi; all other terms are zero. The single-complex and shift comparisons identify L tensor S[degree 1] with a shift of this acyclic complex. The homology exact sequence of step 2 consequently gives that the actual tensor augmentation induces an isomorphism in every degree.

proof_origin.note: The Lean proof implements the one-generator kernel contraction via degreewise splitting and homology exactness, using localization multiplication and the canonical natural sheafification tensor comparison. No K-flat coefficient model, finite-list idempotence theorem, or new postponed theorem is used.

theorem ringed_localization_factor_tensor_augmentation_quasiIso
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    (s : (O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections) :
    letI : IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O)) :=
      SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian _
    letI : CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimitsOfSize.{0, 0} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O)) :=
      CategoryTheory.Limits.hasColimitsOfSizeShrink.{0, 0, u, u} _
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory O
    letI := SheafOfModules.symmetricCategory O
    letI := (SheafOfModules.tensorClosed O).1.some
    letI := (SheafOfModules.tensorClosed O).2.1.some
    letI : ∀ K L : ringedSiteComplex O, HomologicalComplex.HasMapBifunctor K L
        (MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (SheafOfModules.{u}
          ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O))) (.up ℤ) :=
      fun _ _ _ ↦ CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimitsOfShape.has_colimit _
    QuasiIso (HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorMap (𝟙 (ringedLocalizationTwoTerm O s))
      (ringedLocalizationTwoTermAugmentation O s)
      (MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor (SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O))) (.up ℤ))
